state: B1-11 extends Can's typed codecs, running on the pinned Bun 1.4.2 binary, to four more document formats: TOML, YAML, JSON5 and JSONL. Reuse of the proven pipeline is mandatory. A CodecSchema graph generated from the requested result type (leaf kinds str, int, float, bool; composites array, record, error, variant) drives a per-specialization factory; the factory reads a bytes::buffer, enforces standaloneBytes, maxDepth and maxNodes, and projects the native parse result onto immutable Can structure, reporting every deviation as codec::invalid_data with a path and a reason drawn from missing_member, extra_member, type, integer_token, nonfinite, duplicate_member and siblings. Integer fidelity in the decode_json path rests on replaying source numeric tokens instead of consuming lossy doubles. The qualification ledger for the new native entry points records: Bun.TOML.parse fails closed with a losslessness SyntaxError for 9007199254740993 and with a redefinition SyntaxError for doubled keys, while Bun.YAML.parse and Bun.JSON5.parse without complaint emit 9007199254740992 for 9007199254740993 and resolve doubled keys last-wins; nonfinite literals in every parser materialize as real NaN and Infinity numbers; temporal TOML values surface as Temporal objects (PlainDate, PlainDateTime, PlainTime, Instant) whereas temporal YAML scalars surface as strings; YAML applies 1.2 core typing (yes and on parse as strings, all null spellings as null), merges merge keys, aliases share identity, a self-referential anchor can yield a cyclic result, and several documents yield an array; TOML demands a table root but permits mixed arrays; Bun.JSONL.parse maps 9007199254740993 onto 9007199254740992, passes over blank lines, accepts CRLF and an unterminated last line, accepts records broken across lines, and given trailing garbage hands back the valid leading records with neither an error nor a byte count; Bun.JSONL.parseChunk returns values, read, done and error per invocation. Non-negotiable adapter policy: qualified native parsing exclusively, no bespoke document grammars; exactness claims must match one format's declared contract; duplicate policing exists only backed by native evidence.

naming.instructions: Select the catalogue naming approach for the format decoders.

criteria.codec_prefixed: Centralize decoders under codec with format-bearing names that continue the decode_json generic convention across all four formats.
criteria.format_domains: Allocate a dedicated domain per format with a minimal decode operation and a JSONL streaming companion, following the sketch.
criteria.single_decode: Unify decoding behind one generic operation parameterized by a format tag, dispatching to each native parser at runtime.

jsonl_strictness.instructions: Choose the promised JSONL decoding behavior.

criteria.framed_exact: Bounded line splits feed the exact per-record JSON decoder: blanks ignored, CRLF fine, last line may lack its newline, cross-line records invalid, huge integers intact, cut-off input rejected.
criteria.native_whole: Delegate the full text to Bun.JSONL.parse: cross-line records valid, huge integers approximated, trailing junk invisible.
criteria.framed_native: Bound lines structurally but parse each natively: cross-line records invalid, huge integers approximated regardless.

toml_dates.instructions: Decide the fate of TOML temporal values during projection.

criteria.reject_dates: No Temporal value projects: encountering PlainDate, PlainDateTime, PlainTime or Instant aborts with codec::invalid_data at its path.
criteria.project_instant: Instants cross as time::instant where a zone fixes the meaning; zoneless temporal values abort as unrepresentable.
criteria.project_string: Temporal values cross as their ISO-8601 rendering wherever str is expected.
